scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast

scenes.caption: Photo 1892 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: The empire appears to have broken up following the 1076 conquest by the Almoravid General Abu-Bakr Ibn-Umar.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: Archaeological remains found in the coastal zone indicated that the area had been inhabited since the Bronze Age (ca. 2000 BC), but these societies, based on fishing, had left few traces.

scenes.caption: Photo 1892 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: The 9th-century Berber historian and geographer Al Yaqubi described ancient Ghana as one of the three most organized states in the region.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: Ghana succumbed to attacks by its neighbors in the 11th century, but its name and reputation endured.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: According to oral traditions and archaeological evidence, the Dagomba states were the earliest kingdoms to emerge in present-day Ghana as early as the 11th century, being well established by the close of the 16th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: The gold trade, which started to boom in Bonoman as early in the 12th century, was the genesis of Akan power and wealth in the region, beginning in the Middle Ages.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: Under Chief Oti Akenten (r. ca. 1630–60), a series of successful military operations against neighboring Akan states brought a larger surrounding territory into alliance with Ashanti.

scenes.caption: Photo 1892 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: At the end of the 17th century, Osei Tutu became Asantehene (king of Ashanti).

scenes.caption: Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: By the mid-18th century, Ashanti was a highly organized state.

Photo 1890 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: When the first European colonizers arrived in the late 15th century, many inhabitants of the Gold Coast area were striving to consolidate their newly acquired territories and to settle into a secure and permanent environment.

scenes.caption: Photo 1892 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: The Portuguese by 1471 had reached the area that was to become known as the Gold Coast, so named because it was an important source of gold.

scenes.text: The first Ashanti invasion of the coastal regions took place in 1807; the Ashanti moved south again in 1811 and in 1814.

scenes.text: In 1945 a Conference (known as the 5th Pan-African Congress) was held in Manchester to promote Pan-African ideas.

scenes.caption: Photo 1954
scenes.text: Sir Alan Burns' constitution of 1946 established a new legislative council consisting of the Governor as the President, 6 government officials, 6 nominated members and 18 elected members.

scenes.text: On 15 May 1979, less than five weeks before constitutional elections were to be held, a group of junior officers led by Flight Lieutenant Jerry John Rawlings attempted a coup.

scenes.caption: Photo 2010 · Cape Coast
scenes.text: The Constitution entered into force on 7 January 1993, to found the Fourth Republic.

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Between 1050 and 1150, the sources consulted give no precise date.
